themes_detail.label: Lead Contamination Spike
themes_detail.summary: Lead complaints in CD308 surged to 21 THIS WEEK, up 394% from the 8-week average of 4.2 weekly complaints (z-score: 7.95), signaling a possible cluster of unsafe conditions in residential units during peak heating season when lead dust mobilization increases.
evidence: 21 lead complaints THIS WEEK vs. 4.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 7.95)
394% spike occurred during active heating season, when lead dust hazard peaks in older NYC housing stock
CD308 has long-standing budget requests for 'assign additional building inspectors' — persistent gap in enforcement capacity
reporting_angles: Interview families in Crown Heights with children under 6; obtain DOB inspection records for addresses with complaints
Investigate whether NYC's lead remediation funding and inspector capacity are adequate for the scale of this spike; compare to other Brooklyn CDs

themes_detail.label: Noise at Houses of Worship
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints from houses of worship exploded to 4 THIS WEEK, up 3100% from the 8-week average of 0.1 weekly complaints (z-score: 11.72), the highest statistical anomaly in the dataset and suggesting either a new congregation activity, construction, or enforcement shift.
evidence: 4 noise complaints from houses of worship THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 11.72, highest severity)
This is a previously dormant complaint category, suggesting sudden operational change or new conflict
CD308 includes diverse faith communities; concentration of complaints in one week indicates acute, localized trigger
reporting_angles: Identify which specific houses of worship generated complaints; contact them and neighboring residents to understand the triggering event
Explore whether new religious programming, holiday observances, or construction is driving noise; assess complaint legitimacy vs. cultural friction

themes_detail.label: Tree Health & Canopy Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Dead/dying tree complaints hit 6 THIS WEEK (up 1100% from 0.5 weekly average, z-score: 11.0) and new tree requests reached 4 LAST WEEK (up 967% from 0.4 average, z-score: 5.21), indicating possible weather damage, pest outbreak, or disease affecting Crown Heights' street tree canopy.
evidence: 6 dead/dying tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 11.0)
4 new tree requests LAST WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average (z-score: 5.21)
Convergence of two related spikes suggests systemic tree stress; aligns with CB's long-standing budget request for 'park, building, or access improvements'
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Parks to assess whether recent weather (heavy rain, frost, heat stress) triggered mass tree decline in CD308
Map complaint locations; check for common species, age cohort, or pest patterns (e.g., emerald ash borer, longhorned beetles)

themes_detail.label: Elevator Outages Spike
themes_detail.summary: Elevator complaints jumped to 12-15 across two overlapping reporting periods last week (500–243% above 8-week baseline of 0.5–3.5), indicating widespread failures in multi-unit buildings during winter demand peak.
evidence: 12 elevator complaints LAST WEEK vs. 3.5 weekly average (z-score: 5.13, 243% spike)
3 additional elevator reports same period vs. 0.5 baseline (z-score: 5.0, 500% spike)
Particularly acute for elderly and disabled residents; aligns with CB budget priority for 'facilities for homeless' (some residing in buildings) and ongoing housing quality concerns
reporting_angles: Identify buildings with multiple complaint filings; interview residents about repair delays and landlord response
Investigate whether cold weather, deferred maintenance, or sudden surge in commercial/residential foot traffic is driving failures

themes_detail.label: Encampment & Homelessness Clustering
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints reached 3 LAST WEEK, up 1100% from 0.2 weekly average (z-score: 6.35), aligned with CB's repeated budget requests for homeless services expansion, suggesting inadequate shelter/outreach capacity in Crown Heights.
evidence: 3 encampment complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.35, 1100% spike)
CD308 has submitted identical budget requests for 'facilities for homeless' and 'expand street outreach' for multiple years — persistent unmet need
Spike timing coincides with winter surge in homelessness; suggests shelter system strain or outreach failure
reporting_angles: Locate the 3 encampments reported; interview unhoused residents about why they are unsheltered and barriers to services
Request DHS data on shelter bed availability and outreach contacts in CD308; compare to demand signals in 311 data
